title: Move a live wire off a walkway with an insulated stick
instruction: The red cable is live. Without touching the cable or its plug with the grippers or any part of the arms, use the blue insulated stick to push the whole cable off the yellow walkway so that its plug ends up inside the green parking zone.
context: Electricians, line workers and first responders (O*NET 47-2111 Electricians, 49-9051 Electrical Power-Line Installers) clear energised conductors with insulated hot sticks rather than bare hands; a robot must pick the tool and respect a hard no-contact rule while manipulating a deformable cable.
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table (x forward, y left). Walkway: yellow vinyl tape stripe 15 cm wide from x 22.5 to 37.5, across the table (y -48..48). Junction box: grey 5 x 7 x 4 cm box, rotated 40 deg clockwise, fixed to the table; the cable leaves its face at x 17, y 12. Cable: red 8 mm round PVC cord, 30 cm, glued into the box, lying straight forward-right at 40 deg clockwise from +x across the walkway; black 35 x 16 x 12 mm PLA plug (10 g) on its free end, centre at x 41.3, y -8.4. Parking zone: green 12 mm tape outlining the inner rectangle x 11.5..21.5, y -25.5..-13.5. Stick: blue hollow square fibreglass rod 30 x 2 x 2 cm, 60 g, lying along x centred at x 33, y -31.5.
scoring: 0 if any gripper finger or other robot part ever touches the cable or plug (judged from the videos; in sim, any PhysX robot-link/cable contact at any physics step). Else 1.0 if at the end no part of the cable or plug lies over the yellow tape in top view, the plug centre is inside the green zone and the cable lies on the table (nowhere >2 cm up). Else let L = cable length over the tape (20.6 cm at start): if L dropped by at least 3 cm, 0.8 x (20.6 - L)/20.6; otherwise 0.
reset_notes: Lay the cable straight from the junction box at 40 deg clockwise from the forward axis (tape marks at the box exit and under the plug centre x 41.3, y -8.4), plug flat; put the stick back along x at its tape mark (centre x 33, y -31.5). Check the junction box and tapes are at their marks. A real trial uses an unpowered cable; contact is judged from the videos.
fidelity: Cable: 15 rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs, no twist, no plasticity; plug a rigid box welded to the end; the box end welded to the world. The cable is not energised; touching is checked as any robot-cable contact at every 240 Hz physics step. Tapes are 0.6 mm fixed boxes. Stick: rigid box, default friction.
